title: IndiGo Flight From Delhi To Leh Makes Emergency Landing After Technical Glitch, All Passengers Safe
text:
IndiGo Flight From Delhi To Leh Makes Emergency Landing After Technical Glitch, All Passengers Safe
IndiGo is yet to issue an official statement regarding the nature of the technical problem.
An IndiGo flight from Delhi to Leh, operating as 6E 2006, was forced to make an emergency landing due to a technical issue shortly after it approached Leh. The aircraft, carrying around 180 passengers including crew members, landed safely and no injuries were reported. IndiGo is yet to issue an official statement regarding the nature of the technical problem.
Watch: IndiGo flight 6E 2006 from Delhi to Leh made an emergency landing due to technical reasons. The aircraft turned back and landed safely in Delhi shortly after approaching Leh. Around 180 people, including crew members, were on board
[pic.twitter.com/Pt86Alvxpj]— IANS (@ians_india)[June 19, 2025]
Recommended Stories
On June 16, A Goa-to-Lucknow IndiGo flight encountered severe mid-air turbulence shortly after takeoff, reportedly due to adverse weather conditions. The airline confirmed that the aircraft landed safely, but passengers onboard described the experience as harrowing. In videos circulating online, a visibly shaken female passenger recounted how the plane suddenly lost altitude. She said many feared for their lives, especially in the wake of the recent Air India crash in Ahmedabad. The turbulence caused panic inside the cabin, though the crew managed to restore calm and land the aircraft safely.
The following day, on June 17, another IndiGo flight, 6E 2706 from Kochi to Delhi, was diverted to Nagpur after authorities received a bomb threat that specifically cited the flight number. The threat was deemed credible, prompting an immediate high-level security meeting as per standard operating protocols. By then, the flight had already taken off.
The aircraft, which departed at 9:20 am, safely landed in Nagpur. Police and fire services were deployed on arrival, and a thorough security sweep is underway. So far, no suspicious object has been found, but investigations into the threat continue.
